title: Switzerland's $270 Train vs China's Free Duku Highway | China Travel Expert
description:
Switzerland's Glacier Express charges roughly US$270 for its full-fare alpine ride. China's Duku Highway gives you desert-to-glacier drama for the price of fuel.

The Duku (G217) runs about 561 km through Xinjiang, from the Dushanzi badlands up over passes above 3,500 m to alpine meadows and snow. There's no ticket and no toll on the road itself — you only pay for a car and fuel. The catch: it's open only about four months a year, roughly June to October.

🧭 Expert Tip: Drive it June–September, head south from Dushanzi for the best reveals, and start early — gated sections only let vehicles on from the morning.
